key_insight: Jointly optimizing object shapes and poses with physics-aware constraints produces simulation-ready reconstructions of highly cluttered scenes that are more accurate and stable than separate or purely vision-driven pipelines.
problem_solved: Recovers shapes and poses of multiple interacting rigid objects from real-world observations in cluttered, occluded scenes while producing scenes that run stably in physics simulators (real-to-sim), overcoming high cost, brittleness, and limited scalability of prior methods.
method: Unified optimization that jointly estimates object geometry and 6-DoF poses for multiple rigid bodies under physical constraints (contacts, collisions, dynamic stability).
Physics-aware loss terms (contact consistency, penetration avoidance, simulation stability) that guide reconstructions to be ‘simulation-ready’.
An efficient solver/design that handles occlusions and inter-object interactions to scale to cluttered scenes with many objects.
impact: Enables more reliable sim-to-real workflows for planning, control, and policy learning by producing realistic, physically consistent scene models — reducing tuning and failure in downstream robotics and simulation-based training.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input RGB-D / multi-view → joint shape+pose optimization → simulation-validated scene
Before/after scene comparison: noisy partial observations vs. completed simulation-ready reconstruction
Contact & stability overlay: visualizing contact points, penetration correction, and predicted dynamic rollouts
Evaluation charts: accuracy vs. number of objects, simulation stability metric, and runtime comparisons to baselines
paper_title: Simulation-Ready Cluttered Scene Estimation via Physics-aware Joint Shape and Pose Optimization
paper_authors: Wei-Cheng Huang, Jiaheng Han, Xiaohan Ye, Zherong Pan, Kris Hauser
